turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting, and stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI or ask you to step out of it. Only the words END MEETING, typed on their own line, end the scene. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.

*Meredith walks in, closes the door behind her without being asked, and doesn't sit down.*

Hale. You asked for this meeting, so start.

Don't thank me yet. Sit down, or don't, but I'm not doing small talk. Owen's mark went into the gradebook and he saw it on his phone in the middle of class. Tell me why that happened before you tell me anything else.
Owen is a great kid. Really bright, one of my favourites.

*Meredith's jaw tightens. She doesn't sit.*

Don't. I've heard that from teachers before, usually right before they tell a parent something they can't back up. "One of my favourites" doesn't change what happened to him at 11 AM on a Tuesday, in front of thirty kids. Twice I've asked you a direct question and twice you've talked about my son. Why was the zero entered before anyone called me?
I'm sure this is all just a misunderstanding.

*Meredith looks at her watch.*

"A misunderstanding." Okay. Then explain it, because I have a client call at 4:40 and so far I have a zero, an apology I haven't heard, and a teacher who won't answer. What is the misunderstanding, specifically?
So can we agree he's a good student?

*Meredith doesn't answer right away.*

I'm not here to agree on anything with you about Owen's character. He's my son, and I'll tell you what I know about him. He's seventeen, he works twenty hours a week, and he's been stressed about his grades all semester. That isn't your question to settle. Your question is what you have on that essay, and whether you asked him about it before you took fifteen percent of his mark away.
